## The problem

<!-- What you are trying to do and where the library stops you. Lead
with the problem rather than the proposed API: a described problem often
has a solution in the existing surface, and if it does not, the problem
is what the design has to answer to. -->

## What you tried

<!-- Which existing exports, stores, or documents you reached for, and
how far they got. "There is no way to do X" is much stronger when it
lists what was tried. -->

## Where it would live

<!-- Optional. Hosts integrate through three channels only: exported
zustand stores, props and callbacks, and versioned JSON documents. New
capability is exposed through one of those, plus a wiring-guide snippet
and an executable twin in `examples/wiring/`. If you have a view on
which channel fits, say so; if not, that is fine, it is a design
question. -->

## Scope check

<!-- ARCHITECTURE.md draws the line: if an adopter would need to
configure, disable, or replace it, it is application-level and belongs
in `examples/`, not in a published package. If you think this one is
toolkit-level, a sentence on why helps. -->
